title: Meeting Rooms II
description: Compute the fewest rooms needed for all meeting intervals. Each room hosts at most one meeting at a time. A room ending a meeting at time t is available to another meeting starting at t.

examples.explain: Two rooms cover the overlap; the third meeting reuses a freed room.
examples.raw:
Input: intervals = [[0,40],[5,10],[15,20]]
Output: 2
Explanation: Two rooms cover the overlap; the third meeting reuses a freed room.

examples.explain: A single meeting needs one room.
examples.raw:
Input: intervals = [[4,9]]
Output: 1
Explanation: A single meeting needs one room.

hints: Sort by start and track running end times in a min-heap.
Free every room whose meeting ended at or before the next start.
The heap size after processing is the answer; an empty schedule needs zero.
solution: Sweep starts in order with a min-heap of end times, freeing rooms as meetings end. Peak heap size is the room count.
